title: Cohomology of a local integral perfect scalar model
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ and $S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $g:S\hookrightarrow X$ a locally closed immersion, that is, a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion]. On the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\pi^n)_T$ for $T=X,S$, using constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The projection maps give a canonical isomorphism $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\xrightarrow{\sim}B_S$, where inverse image is [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define $g^*$ on module sheaves by inverse image followed by scalar extension along $c_g$. This functor is exact, as is restriction $j_U^*$ to the localized ringed site of any object $U$ of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$, and let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, representing a perfect scalar complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Write $T_U(M)=j_U^*(B_S\otimes_{R_S}M_S)$ for scalar extension of the constant module sheaf with value an $R$-module $M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply the exact restriction functors termwise on derived categories. If an isomorphism $j_U^*g^*K\simeq T_U(P^\bullet)$ is given, then, for every integer $q$, $H^q(P^\bullet)$ is finitely presented over $R$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] and that isomorphism induces an isomorphism
$$j_U^*g^*H^q(K)\simeq T_U(H^q(P^\bullet)).$$
No Noetherianity, dimension or residue-characteristic hypothesis on $X$ or $S$ is imposed. There is no assumption of derived completeness on $K$, nor a global constructibility conclusion.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), final sentence: the cohomology calculation implicit in the application of Proposition 6.6.11. Supporting exactness is Stacks Tag 09AA (proetale.tex, lemma-closed-immersion), Tags 093J and 093M (sites-modules.tex, lemma-constant-exact and lemma-completion-flat); scalar finiteness is Tag 00IK (algebra.tex, lemma-Noetherian-basic).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](2), the coefficient ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ is a principal ideal domain. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] to conclude that $R$ is Noetherian. This is a condition on the scalar ring alone; it imposes no condition on either scheme.

source.place: Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), scalar Noetherian hypothesis; the DVR coefficient convention is def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] canonically identifies $g^{-1}(R/\pi^n)_X$ with $(R/\pi^n)_S$. The reduction maps agree under these identifications: a constant scalar $a\bmod\pi^{n+1}$ maps to the constant scalar $a\bmod\pi^n$ on both sites. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], $g^{-1}$ preserves this small countable inverse limit. Thus the map characterized by the quotient projections is the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\simeq B_S$; it respects addition and multiplication because each quotient projection does. The same lemma, with this $c_g$, makes $g^*$ exact. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], $j_U^*$ is exact for every site object $U$, so their composite $F=j_U^*g^*$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), clause (1), and open localized-site restriction; module slice restriction is Tag 03DJ (sites-modules.tex, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact).

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties], taking the constant $R$-module sheaf preserves short exact sequences (even after taking sections on every object). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-algebra-flat-quotients] on $S$ with $A=R$, $I=(\pi)$, and with its specified presentation equal to $B_S$ itself. Its tower indexed by $n\geq0$ is the same tower $(R/\pi^{n+1})_S$ as the one here indexed by positive integers. The canonical $R_S\to B_S$ has precisely the required reduction composites, so that lemma supplies exact scalar extension to $B_S$-modules. Composing it with constant realization and the exact restriction of step 2 proves that $T_U:M\mapsto j_U^*(B_S\otimes_{R_S}M_S)$ is exact.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact functors $F$ and $T_U$: their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and compute their induced functors on unbounded derived categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], there are natural isomorphisms $H^q(FK)\simeq F(H^qK)$ and $H^q(T_U(P^\bullet))\simeq T_U(H^q(P^\bullet))$. Given the specified model isomorphism $\alpha:FK\simeq T_U(P^\bullet)$, apply the cohomology functor to $\alpha$ and its inverse. They remain inverse maps. The composite
$$F(H^qK)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(FK)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(T_U(P^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}T_U(H^q(P^\bullet))$$
is therefore the asserted isomorphism, with the first arrow the inverse of the exact-functor cohomology comparison. No completeness or boundedness of $K$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), final sentence via Proposition 6.6.11: explicit local cohomology calculation; exact-functor descent is Stacks Tag 015F (derived.tex, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor).

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$. The term $P^q$ is finitely generated by hypothesis and $R$ is Noetherian by step 1. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes its submodule $Z^q=\ker(d^q:P^q\to P^{q+1})$ finitely generated. The identity $d^q d^{q-1}=0$ places $\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ in $Z^q$, and the images of a finite generating set of $Z^q$ generate its quotient $H^q(P^\bullet)=Z^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] to this finite $R$-module to obtain finite presentation. This applies also when the term or cohomology is zero and permits torsion cohomology.

source.place: Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), first two assertions: finite modules are finitely presented and their submodules are finite.

tool_uses.why: Coefficient algebra: its PID assertion supplies the Noetherian scalar hypothesis; it does not replace any integral-model unit step.
Generic geometric inverse image of constant rings identifies each finite quotient and its scalar sections; the unit has no separate constant inverse-image statement.
Generic locally closed pro-étale inverse image preserves the coefficient limit and is exact with identified coefficients; no Noetherian scheme assumption is introduced.
Generic exactness of restriction to a localized ringed site is needed for arbitrary U; it is not an integral constructibility argument.
Its first clause gives exact constant module realization, a generic site fact not supplied by the integral-model unit.
Generic completion-flatness supplies exact scalar extension from the constant R-sheaf to its explicit inverse-limit ring; this is exactly the unit route’s flat coefficient map.

Step 3: clause (1) of constant-module-section-properties (R Noetherian) and completed-constant-algebra-flat-quotients (its B is literally B_S, A=R, I=(π)) give exact T_U.
